title: seek shared configuration definitions
description: The shapes both seek configuration files share: a secret source, the provider keys, and the Vault or OpenBao connection. The client and server schemas refer to these definitions.

secret.description: Where seek reads one secret. Set exactly one of `value`, `file`, `command` or `vault`.

local-secret.description: Where seek reads a credential it uses to reach Vault or OpenBao. Set exactly one of `value`, `file` or `command`.

value.description: The secret itself, with surrounding whitespace removed. `seek config show` prints it as `<redacted>`. It has an environment variable and no flag.

file.description: Path of a file that holds the secret, such as a container secret mount or a systemd credential. seek removes surrounding whitespace from its content. A leading `~/` is the home directory; another relative path in a configuration file is relative to that file's directory.

command.description: A credential helper and its arguments, as an array. seek runs it without a shell, in the directory of the configuration file that declared it, and reads the secret from its standard output, trimmed. A non-zero exit status is a failure. Errors and `seek config show` name only the program, its first element, and the number of arguments. As an environment variable or flag, the array is JSON.

timeout.description: How long seek waits for the helper before it stops it and fails.

vault-secret.description: One field of a Vault or OpenBao KV secret. `path` and `key` are required. Each other field it leaves unset takes the merged top-level `vault` setting.

path.description: Path of the KV secret within its mount. Leading and trailing slashes are removed; an empty, `.` or `..` segment is invalid.

key.description: Field of the KV secret that holds the value.

vault.description: Defaults for every `vault` secret source in this configuration: the server, its namespace, the KV mount and version, the certificate authority, the proxy and the authentication. A secret's own `vault` block overrides each field it sets, and a secret with its own `auth` takes none of this one.

vault-address.description: Address of the Vault or OpenBao server: an `https://` or `http://` URL, which may end in a base path such as `/team-a`, or `unix://` followed by the absolute path of a socket. It carries no user name, password, query or fragment. Trailing slashes are removed, and request routes are appended under the base path.

vault-namespace.description: Vault or OpenBao namespace, sent as the `X-Vault-Namespace` header. An empty string selects the root namespace: no header is sent, and no top-level or exported namespace is filled in.

vault-mount.description: Mount of the KV secrets engine. Leading and trailing slashes are removed; an empty, `.` or `..` segment is invalid.

vault-kv-version.description: Version of the KV secrets engine.

vault-ca-cert.description: Path of a PEM bundle of the certificate authorities seek trusts for this server. It replaces Bun's whole default store: its bundled roots, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` and, with `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1`, the system store. A leading `~/` is the home directory; another relative path in a configuration file is relative to that file's directory.

vault-auth.description: How seek authenticates to the server. `mode` selects the method and is required. An `auth` mapping is used only for the server in effect where it was declared, as the configuration specification describes.

token.description: The Vault or OpenBao token. A `file` token is read again before each secret read, so a token that an agent rotates takes effect without a restart.

mount.description: Mount of the AppRole auth method. Leading and trailing slashes are removed; an empty, `.` or `..` segment is invalid.

role-id.description: AppRole role ID. `seek config show` prints it as `<redacted>`.

mode.description: Send no token, for a server that needs none, such as an agent socket that authenticates the connection itself.

providers.description: The API key of each provider seek calls, keyed by upstream ID.

api-key.description: Parallel API key, used by `seek web parallel`, `seek research parallel` and `seek scrape parallel`, and sent to Parallel as the `x-api-key` header.
Exa API key, used by `seek web exa` and `seek scrape exa`, and sent to Exa as the `x-api-key` header.
Brave Search API key, used by `seek web brave search`, and sent to Brave as the `X-Subscription-Token` header.
Brave Answers API key, used by `seek web brave answers`, `seek research brave` and the Brave planner of `seek research google --interactive`, and sent to Brave as the `X-Subscription-Token` header.

Perplexity API key, used by `seek web perplexity`, `seek research perplexity` and the Perplexity planner of `seek research google --interactive`, and sent to Perplexity as an `Authorization: Bearer` header.
Google Gemini API key, used by `seek research google`, and sent to Google as the `x-goog-api-key` header.
Firecrawl API key, used by `seek scrape firecrawl`, and sent to Firecrawl as an `Authorization: Bearer` header.

duration.description: A duration: a whole number followed by `ms`, `s`, `m` or `h`.

vault-proxy.description: HTTP proxy for this server's requests, as an `http://` or `https://` URL with a host and optional port only; it carries no user name, password, path, query or fragment, and seek sends no proxy credentials, as the operator decided in `authenticated-vault-proxy`. Without it seek connects directly and ignores `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY`.
